problem: VLM-based navigators output low-level atomic actions or regress 3D coordinates (a geometric gap with 2D-pretrained VLMs), reason at every step or fixed intervals (high latency), and use memory that either overflows or discards key information and lacks spatio-temporal structure.
motivation: Deploying VLMs for real-world navigation needs accurate geometry-grounded actions, low inference latency and long-horizon memory. The authors argue VLMs' 2D priors are best used by pointing at pixels, reasoning is only needed at critical nodes, and non-critical steps still carry spatio-temporal transition information worth keeping cheaply.
key_idea: Have a Qwen2.5-VL agent point at 2D pixels (projected to 3D for a SLAM controller), reason only at critical nodes stored as explicit anchors with lightweight space-time indicator tokens in between, and align it with a Two-Level GRPO combining trajectory-level and step-level advantages.
insight: Ablations show the action formulation matters most: replacing Pixel-to-3D with a NavFoM-style metric waypoint drops R2R-CE SR from 55.7 to 30.9 (SFT-only). RL with dense local rewards adds a lot (SFT 55.7 to 66.2 SR), with local advantages giving +4.1 SR over trajectory-only GRPO and annealed guidance +2.8 more. Selective CoT (26.3% ratio) nearly matches dense CoT (66.2 vs 66.8 SR) while fixed 1/3 interval reasoning drops to 60.1, so learned timing matters; CoT teacher quality also matters (weak 7B CoT is worse than no CoT).
method: Pixel-to-3D Action: from four egocentric views the VLM picks a view and outputs a 2D pixel; it is back-projected with depth and intrinsics to a 3D waypoint and executed by a SLAM controller (FAR planner + FastLIO in the real world)

Anchor-Trajectory Memory: CoT-triggered nodes stored as Explicit Anchors (STI token, raw visual features, CoT task-phase summary); intermediate path intervals kept only as STI tokens; context also includes two working-memory frames
Space-Time Indicator (STI) token: 2D RoPE(x,y), 1D RoPE(t) and RoPE(sin yaw, cos yaw), concatenated and projected by an MLP into one token

MultiNav-CoT dataset: 90k VLN-CE trajectories; key nodes (~30%) mined by CLIP semantic + visual-transition scores with distance-based greedy filtering (D_min=2, D_max=6) and temporal padding; CoT generated by Gemini 2.5 Flash in staged prompts

Two-Level GRPO: G=8 trajectories, each step samples M=4 candidates; the executed one is chosen by softmax over local reward with annealed beta; advantage = Z-scored global trajectory advantage + Z-scored local step advantage
Dual rewards: local (approach, collision, stop, reasoning value, format) and global (success, SPL, reasoning density), after SFT cold start on Qwen2.5-VL-7B

setting.training_data: MultiNav-CoT: 90k VLN-CE trajectories (~700k interactions) with Gemini 2.5 Flash CoT, plus ~10% GQA interleaved-CoT for SFT; then GRPO for 800 steps in Habitat on the same data
setting.observation: four egocentric RGB-D views covering 360° plus pose (x,y,yaw,t) for STI
setting.action_space: 2D pixel on a selected view, projected to a 3D waypoint and executed by a SLAM local planner
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT depth in simulation; GRPO training uses simulator signals such as geodesic distance and obstacle distance)

numbers.extra: SFT+Two-Level GRPO; 90k trajectories; GT depth in simulation

numbers_note: Real-world results (SR 60.0% for TAMP-Nav vs StreamVLN 49.0% and DualVLN 53.0%, 100 trials each) are reported only in a figure and the text; not a standard benchmark.
results: TAMP-Nav achieves 66.2 SR / 58.8 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen and 65.7 SR / 56.9 SPL on RxR-CE val-unseen, beating DualVLN (64.3 SR) and NavFoM (64.4 RxR SR). It uses ~9 steps per trajectory and 16.58 s per task vs 37.47 s (StreamVLN) and 41.46 s (DualVLN), and reaches 49.8 SR on long-horizon episodes vs 41.9 for DualVLN.
limitations: Depends on depth and a reliable SLAM stack; drift, localization failure and dynamic scenes can degrade performance
GRPO relies on privileged simulator signals, so there is no online RL on real robots and real-world transfer is zero-shot only
STI encodes only planar pose (no height, so it cannot distinguish floors); key-node heuristic and reasoning-density thresholds are tuned to R2R-CE/RxR-CE
